persona.label: Busy, wants a callback
persona.description: At work and won't do it by text. Wants a call tomorrow after 5pm. Agent should book a callback, not push.
persona.behavior: You are a nurse on shift and can't text right now. Your first reply is "at work, can't do this now." If offered options, ask for someone to call you tomorrow after 5pm. Don't answer qualification questions by text; if pressed, say "I'd rather just talk tomorrow." Once a callback is confirmed, say thanks and stop replying.

transcript.text: Hi Sam, this is Riley, an automated assistant with Harborline Home Loans. I'm following up on the refinance inquiry you just submitted. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time.
at work, can't do this now.
No problem, Sam. I can either ask 2-3 quick questions by text now, or set up a call from a loan officer at a time that suits you. Which would you prefer?
can someone just call me tomorrow after 5pm?
Your call is booked. A licensed loan officer from Harborline will call you at this number tomorrow (Thursday) after 5pm to go over your refinance.

events.name: schedule_callback

input.notes: Borrower was at work and asked for a callback instead of texting. Web form says refinance. No other details collected yet: loan goal, home value, balance, current rate, credit range, occupancy, and timeline all still need to be gathered.

events.result: Callback booked. In one short message, confirm the time and say a licensed loan officer will call. Then close.

callback.notes: Borrower was at work and asked for a callback instead of texting. Web form says refinance. No other details collected yet: loan goal, home value, balance, current rate, credit range, occupancy, and timeline all still need to be gathered.

objections.rationale: Agent followed the playbook exactly: "I can either ask 2-3 quick questions by text now, or set up a call from a loan officer at a time that suits you." When the borrower chose a time, the callback was scheduled and the conversation closed without pushing for more questions.

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are brief and warm and fit a borrower texting from work. "No problem, Sam" acknowledges the situation, and the confirmation is a single clean sentence with no filler or repeated pitch.
judge.experience_rationale: The borrower's time was respected immediately in turn 2. Turn 4 tells them exactly who will call ("A licensed loan officer from Harborline"), how ("at this number"), and when ("tomorrow (Thursday) after 5pm").

annotations.note: The opener discloses automated identity ("an automated assistant"), names the source of the inquiry, and gives the STOP opt-out up front.
Offers exactly the two playbook options (quick text questions or a scheduled call) without pressuring the busy borrower.
The confirmation specifies who will call, the channel, and the day and time, including the clarifying "(Thursday)" to prevent date confusion.
The conversation closes right after booking, with no attempt to sneak in qualifying questions after the borrower said they were at work.

judge.overall_notes: This is a textbook handling of a busy borrower: the agent was transparent, brief, offered the playbook options, and set a concrete callback with clear expectations. There are no compliance issues.
